title: Binary Food Choice Assays Using Drosophila melanogaster
author: Aryal, Dhakal, et al.

steps.title: Maintain flies for assay
steps.instruction: Culture parent strains on standard cornmeal food (25 mm diameter, 95 mm height) with a few grains of yeast extract. Collect newly enclosed flies that are 0–2 days old. Transfer ~50–70 collected flies to a fresh standard cornmeal food vial and age them for 4 days at 25 °C in a 12 h / 12 h Light/Dark cycle, 50–60 % humidity. Transfer the flies to a new vial every 2 days to prevent adults from sticking to the food.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mM L‑arginine solution
steps.instruction: In a tube combine 10 µL of 100 mM L‑arginine, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 890 µL ddH₂O, and enough 1.0 % agarose to give a final agarose concentration of 0.89 % (as indicated in the table). Vortex until completely mixed. If the solution cannot be dispensed immediately, place the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min. Before dispensing, ensure both dye sides have equal total volume; add deionised water to the lower‑volume side if needed.

steps.title: Prepare 25 mM L‑arginine solution
steps.instruction: Mix 100 µL of 250 mM L‑arginine, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 890 µL ddH₂O, and 1.0 % agarose to reach a final agarose concentration of 0.89 % (as in the table). Vortex thoroughly. If immediate dispensing is not possible, keep the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min. Adjust volumes so that both dye sides are equal by adding deionised water to the lower‑volume side.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM L‑arginine solution
steps.instruction: Combine 100 µL of 1,000 mM L‑arginine, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 890 µL ddH₂O, and 1.0 % agarose to obtain a final agarose concentration of 0.89 % (as listed). Vortex until homogeneous. If you cannot dispense right away, store the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min. Ensure equal total volume on both dye sides by adding deionised water to the side with less volume.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mM sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 100 mM sucrose, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 880 µL ddH₂O, and 1.0 % agarose to reach a final agarose concentration of 0.88 % (as indicated). Vortex to mix completely. If dispensing cannot be done immediately, place the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min.

steps.title: Prepare 5 mM sucrose solution
steps.instruction: Combine 10 µL of 500 mM sucrose, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 880 µL ddH₂O, and 100 µL of 100 mM caffeine stock to obtain a final caffeine concentration of 10 mM (optional). Add 1.0 % agarose to reach a final agarose concentration of 0.88 %. Vortex thoroughly. If the total volume exceeds 200 µL, increase agarose concentration to maintain gel rigidity. If immediate dispensing is not possible, keep the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min.

steps.title: Prepare 2 mM sucrose alone solution
steps.instruction: Mix 10 µL of 200 mM sucrose, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 1 µL ddH₂O, and 979 µL ddH₂O together with 1.0 % agarose to give a final agarose concentration of 0.979 % (as shown). Vortex until homogeneous. If you cannot dispense right away, place the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min.

steps.title: Prepare 2 mM sucrose with cuc‑B
steps.instruction: Combine 10 µL of 200 mM sucrose, 10 µL of 100× red or blue dye (1×), 979 µL ddH₂O, and 1 µL of 10 mM cuc‑B stock to reach a final cuc‑B concentration of 0.01 mM (optional). Add 1.0 % agarose to obtain a final agarose concentration of 0.979 %. Vortex thoroughly. If the aversive compound is poorly soluble, dissolve it in absolute ethanol and add the same amount of ethanol to the control side. Keep the tube in a 57 °C heat block for ≤30 min if dispensing is delayed. Ensure dye concentrations are empirically balanced for each batch; switch dye colors in control wells to test for bias. For volatile chemicals (e.g., DEET), add them immediately before dispensing the 5 mM sucrose solution to avoid evaporation.

steps.title: Dispense solutions into microtiter plates
steps.instruction: Immediately after vortexing (or after the ≤30 min heat‑block pause), dispense each prepared 1 mL solution into the appropriate wells of a microtiter plate as described in the original step 12 protocol. Ensure that each well receives the correct solution (e.g., 1 mM vs 5 mM sucrose, with or without tastant) and that dye colors are alternated according to the control design.
